name: Vishal Mega Mart Ltd.
business_summary: Value-retail chain (about 844 stores per Kalkine, Q2 FY27) selling apparel, general merchandise and FMCG/grocery to middle- and lower-income households, largely in tier-2/3 India. TTM sales Rs 13,910 cr (+18%), EBITDA Rs 1,987 cr (14.3%), profit Rs 897 cr. Sep-26 quarter: sales Rs 3,399 cr (+14%), OPM 12% (13% year ago), PAT Rs 158 cr (+4% y/y); festive timing shift into Q3 hurt SSSG and margin. Stock Rs 94 (-34% 12m, 52-week low on 2026-10-21/22). Promoters (Samayat, Kedaara-backed, model knowledge) 40.02%, FIIs falling 22.0% -> 18.8%, DIIs 36.5%.

exposures.mechanism: Mass-market urban and semi-urban households: +5pp urban growth -> +4pp sales x 25% contribution on Rs 13,910 cr = Rs 139 cr = 7.0% of EBITDA Rs 1,987 cr; EV/MCap 1.05; persistence 0.5 => +3.7, trimmed to 3.5.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 per Business Standard 2026-10-21 and screener pack

exposures.mechanism: Tier-2/3 customer base (about 75% of stores outside metros, model estimate): +5pp rural/small-town growth -> +3pp sales x 25% = Rs 104 cr = 5.2% EBITDA x 0.5 x 1.05 => +2.7 to +3.

evidence.note: Q2/H1 FY27 financials per screener.in pack; cost shares are model estimates unless stated

exposures.mechanism: Customer wage growth drives mass-market spending; +2pp wages -> +2pp sales (Rs 280 cr x 25% = Rs 70 cr = 3.5% EBITDA x 0.5 x 1.05 => +1.8) minus employee cost drag.

evidence.note: Q2/H1 FY27 financials per screener.in pack; cost shares are model estimates unless stated

exposures.mechanism: +2pp food inflation squeezes discretionary wallet of low-income households (FMCG/grocery is ~30% of sales but low margin): -1% sales on discretionary at 25% = ~Rs 35 cr = 1.8% EBITDA... scaled => -1.5.

evidence.note: Q2/H1 FY27 financials per screener.in pack; cost shares are model estimates unless stated

exposures.mechanism: Empirical -1.47/SSU (t=-2.8) - significant. Mechanism: logistics/diesel/plastics ~5% of costs (Rs 600 cr; +10% Brent -> +3% = 1% EBITDA) plus low-income households' fuel/LPG budget squeezed (demand channel); combined ~-1.0, weaker than the empirical.
Empirical -1.26 (t=-2.6); likely a second proxy for the energy-price/household-budget channel already in F_BRENT, so only -0.6 retained to avoid double counting.
Cotton-linked apparel inputs ~6% of Rs 11,923 cr costs; +10% cotton -> +6% garment cost = Rs 43 cr = 2.2% of EBITDA x 0.6 unrecovered x persistence 0.3 => -0.4.

evidence.note: Q2/H1 FY27 financials per screener.in pack; cost shares are model estimates unless stated

exposures.mechanism: Imports ~5% of COGS (electronics, some apparel, toys): +3% -> Rs 28 cr = 1.4% EBITDA x 0.6 x 0.5 => -0.25. Empirical +2.36 (t=+1.7) has the opposite sign (market-beta artefact), so the range includes positive values.

Low-price apparel/FMCG already benefited from Sept-2025 rationalisation (model knowledge); another broad cut (+1) lifts volumes ~3% => +2.5. Probability low after 2026-10-08 Council with no rate cuts.
Trent's Zudio (22% growth), Reliance, Max, DMart and e-commerce compete for the same household; +1 cuts SSSG ~1.5pp or margin 70 bp (~5% EBITDA) x persistence 0.4 => -2.

evidence.note: Q2/H1 FY27 financials per screener.in pack; cost shares are model estimates unless stated

exposures.mechanism: Quick commerce takes staples, general merchandise and basic baskets from stores in metros; small share of VMM sales: -1.

exposures.mechanism: 49x trailing P/E; leases dominate interest (Rs 183 cr TTM): +25 bp repo -> -2% fair value, half transmitted => -1.0.
